title: Four-dimensional quantum Yang–Mills existence and mass gap
decision_reason: CMI still labels the problem unsolved, but Nielsen’s February 2026 manuscript abstract claims the matching continuum construction and gap for compact simple non-Abelian groups. Full access and specialist adjudication of that manuscript are unresolved; do not count it as accepted.

problem_fingerprint.model_or_objects: Nontrivial pure quantum Yang–Mills field with compact simple gauge group G
problem_fingerprint.domain: R^4, not a fixed lattice or finite torus
problem_fingerprint.regularity_and_data_class: Operator-valued distributions with Wightman or equivalent OS axioms and prescribed ultraviolet behavior
problem_fingerprint.quantifiers: For every G exists a nontrivial theory and Delta>0
problem_fingerprint.limit_regime_and_order: Any regularization must yield the full continuum infinite-volume theory
problem_fingerprint.computational_model_and_dependencies: Unconditional construction, not numerical evidence or a postulated effective Hamiltonian

statement_source_and_scope_match: Jaffe–Witten official description §§3–4, printed pp. 5–6, specifies quantum-field axioms, local curvature observables, short-distance behavior, and finite positive mass gap.
proposed_statement_text: For every compact simple gauge group G, construct a nontrivial quantum Yang–Mills theory on R^4 with axioms at least as strong as Wightman/Osterwalder–Schrader, the prescribed short-distance behavior, and Hamiltonian spectrum disjoint from (0,Delta) for some Delta>0, with finite supremal gap.
applied_significance: Seeks a rigorous continuum foundation for the gauge-field description of fundamental interactions and the positive excitation-energy scale suggested by pure strong-interaction models.
